name: timedatectl
description: Shows and sets system time, timezone, and NTP synchronization.

examples.output:
Local time: Sat 2025-01-12 10:14:01 CET
           Universal time: Sat 2025-01-12 09:14:01 UTC
                 Time zone: Europe/Berlin (CET, +0100)
 System clock synchronized: yes
               NTP service: active
examples.explanation: Everything about the clock in one view. "synchronized: yes" means NTP is keeping it accurate.
Switches the server to UTC — best practice for servers so logs align across timezones.
Enables NTP via systemd-timesyncd. A wrong clock breaks TLS certificates and Kerberos.

about: Correct time matters more than most admins expect: TLS certificate validation, cron jobs, log correlation, and Kerberos all break with clock drift. systemd-timesyncd is a lightweight SNTP client; chrony or ntpd are used when more accuracy is needed.
mistakes: Setting the timezone but not checking that NTP is active — the clock will drift again.
